title: Add Go RAG agent quickstart and tool-calling sample + docs site example
author: Aisha Patel
description: Adds a new Go quickstart demonstrating a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) agent that uses Redwood's tool-calling capability to query an external vector store and run deterministic tools for structured lookups. Motivation: provide a minimal, idiomatic Go example for teams that want an agent-based RAG pattern with explicit tool contracts and a docs site snippet. Changes include a self-contained example under examples/go/rag-agent, a small helper library (examples/go/rag-agent/pkg) for tool adapters, a CI job to run the example's smoke tests in GitHub Actions, and a docs site snippet that can be embedded in the 'Getting started: Agents' page. Checklist: 1) Example program + README with quickstart and expected output; 2) reusable tool adapter interface and two sample adapters (vector-store mock, deterministic lookup tool); 3) unit and smoke tests that run in CI; 4) docs snippet and screenshots for the docs site; 5) basic lint/format fixes. This is intended to be a beginner-friendly starting point — it uses the hosted Redwood API by default but includes configuration for local/private endpoints and API key injection. Security note: the example uses a local in-memory index for testing; provide guidance in README for production-grade vector stores and KMS usage. Migration notes: no API changes to SDKs, strictly an examples/docs addition. See files_changed for details and the commits below for iteration history.

The example defaults to the hosted API for convenience but includes clear environment variables for private endpoints and KMS guidance. If backporting to release branches, only cherry-pick the docs snippet if the site generator matches the template version.
user_testing_instructions: Clone the repo, cd examples/go/rag-agent, go test ./... to run unit tests, then go run main.go with REDWOOD_API_KEY set to run the smoke example. The README contains step-by-step instructions and expected sample output. To run against a private deployment set REDWOOD_API_HOST and REDWOOD_API_KEY accordingly.
impact_assessment: Low: example and docs only. CI added to run non-production smoke tests. No runtime, SDK, or public API changes. Recommended reviewers: docs, examples maintainers, and Go SDK owner to confirm idiomatic usage.
